https://business-review.eu/tech/it/innov.text: Innovation, feasibility and relevance among key project evaluation criteria at NASA Space Apps Challenge The competition brings together programmers, scientists, designers, engineers, university students and high school students, who will work in teams to develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges related to Earth and space, using open data provided by NASA and its partner space agencies. “I absolutely love the energy at NASA Space Apps: 48 intense hours, coffee, and people building things they would otherwise spend months planning. As a judge, I’m not looking for the most polished pitch. I’m looking for teams that start with a problem, test their ideas against real data, and can clearly explain why their work matters. Creativity can take you a long way, but it’s the data that turns it into a solution that stands up beyond the demo,” says Aleodor Tabarcea, Site Lead & Engineering Manager at Stripe and judge at the Bucharest edition of NASA Space Apps Challenge. Projects developed by participants – ranging from web and mobile applications, educational games and software tools to AI-powered solutions, data visualizations and engineering prototypes – will be assessed on a scale of 1 to 5 across five criteria. Impact measures the solution’s ability to address a real-world problem and generate benefits for the community. Creativity focuses on the originality of the idea and the innovative nature of the approach. Validity assesses the scientific foundation, technical feasibility and practical applicability of the solution. Relevance evaluates how well the project addresses the requirements of the selected challenge and makes meaningful use of NASA data. Presentation assesses the clarity and structure of the project, as well as the team’s ability to communicate the identified problem, proposed solution and its impact through a compelling narrative. Read more about Five projects from Bucharest and Cluj have qualified for global stage of NASA Space Apps Challenge read more “NASA Space Apps Challenge demonstrates how data and technology can become the starting point for solutions to real-world problems. From MetaMinds’ perspective, a valuable project is one that starts with a creative idea, supports it with a solid technical approach, and succeeds in turning it into a relevant solution. I’m looking forward to seeing how the teams tackle the proposed challenges, how they leverage the resources made available by NASA and, above all, how they manage to take their ideas beyond the concept stage. Beyond the final outcome, initiatives like this bring together people with complementary expertise and create opportunities for learning and collaboration,” says Ovidiu Ghiman, CEO of MetaMinds, partner of this year’s NASA Space Apps Challenge. The Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca editions bring together specialists from technology companies, startups and academic institutions, who will provide participants with technical guidance and feedback on their projects. “We are delighted to support young people through education, AI tools and internationally recognized certifications. At NASA Space Apps, participants have just 48 hours to develop technological solutions based on real data provided by NASA. AI can give these talented young people ‘superpowers’, helping them turn a good idea into a working prototype, even within such a short timeframe,” says Dan Oros, COM Google Central and Eastern Europe, partner of this year’s NASA Space Apps Challenge. Among the mentors and special guests at the Bucharest edition are Adrian Șonka, astronomer at the “Amiral Vasile Urseanu” Astronomical Observatory; Ulpia Botezatu, Co-Chair of the UN Action Team on Lunar Activities Consultations (ATLAC); Mădălina Pană, Software Engineer at Microsoft; Diana Nițescu, cybersecurity policy consultant and founder of octogonHUB; Constantin Levențiu, Deputy Dean of the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering at the National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest; Alex Bordei, technology and AI expert at Whiz Center; and Dmitry Elisov, Insider Risk & Workforce Intelligence specialist at Teramind. Representatives from Stripe, MetaMinds, UiPath, the National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest and the Romanian-American University in Bucharest will also be among the guests and specialists involved in the event. In Cluj-Napoca, the announced mentors include Călin Neamțu, Director of the Design Engineering and Robotics Department at the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca; Hans Christian Johrend, Founder of Wired; Alexandru Coman, Co-founder of YUBA; Andrei Voic, AI Engineer at RebelDot; Kinga Hening, Head of the TechTransfer Center at Babeș-Bolyai University in Cluj-Napoca; and Szilárd Kacsó, Founder of Leadership Architecture. Judging will take place on November 15. The jury for the Bucharest edition includes Costel Negricea – Rector of the Romanian-American University; Aleodor Tabarcea – Engineering Manager at Stripe; Daniel-Eugeniu Crunțeanu – Dean of the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering at the National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest and President of the Romanian Space Agency (ROSA); Constantin Levențiu – Deputy Dean of the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering at the National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest; Dmitry Elisov – Insider Risk & Workforce Intelligence specialist at Teramind; and Adina Zara – Managing Partner at Igodemy. The Cluj-Napoca jury includes Lorand R. Minyo, Founder of Minyo & Co; Bogdan Popovici, Business System Analyst at regnology; Dragos Dușe, Founder of Synaptiq; and Ovidiu Rațiu, Founder of Control Data Systems. Following the local judging process, at least three projects from Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca will be selected to advance to the global stage. The number of teams qualifying for the global stage will be determined based on the number of projects registered on the NASA Space Apps platform. At the international level, judges will evaluate projects submitted from around the world and select winners in 10 categories: Best Use of Science, Best Use of Data, Best Use of Technology, Galactic Impact, Best Concept, Most Inspirational Project, Best Storytelling, Global Connection, Art & Technology, and Local Impact. The globally winning teams will have the opportunity to visit a NASA center or facility, where they will receive their awards and discover the agency’s latest achievements. NASA Space Apps Challenge is open to anyone passionate about Earth and space sciences, regardless of age or professional background. Participants work in multidisciplinary teams over a 48-hour period, combining science, technology and data analysis to address the proposed challenges. More than 487,000 people from 190 countries and territories around the world have taken part in the hackathon’s 14 editions. In Bucharest, the event will take place at the Romanian-American University, while in Cluj-Napoca it will be hosted at ClujHub. Partners of this year’s edition include: Stripe; MetaMinds; UiPath; Google; Youni Choice; the Romanian-American University in Bucharest; the Romanian Space Agency (ROSA); the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering at the National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest; the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca; Babeș-Bolyai University TechTransfer; Parsimoni; Techcelerator; Startup Reaktor; Brick Depot; Cluj RacingPoint; and Codemy. Food & beverage sponsors: Origo, Artesana, Iezeres, Mogyi and Vitamin Aqua. Media partners: Euronews and Revista Știință & Tehnică. Google is offering participants access to the Google AI Professional Certificate specialization course, available on the Coursera learning platform. UiPath is providing vouchers for UiPath certifications to the winners. Parsimoni is offering up to 10 NASA Space Apps Challenge participants worldwide the opportunity to submit their software applications to space free of charge. In Romania, the world’s largest hackathon is organized by DiFine PR, ROTSA, and ClujHub. The first edition of NASA Space Apps Challenge in Romania took place in 2016. NASA International Space Apps Challenge (Space Apps) is an international hackathon for programmers, scientists, designers, storytellers, creators, builders and technology specialists. During the hackathon, teams in cities around the world use publicly available data from NASA (the National Aeronautics and Space Administration) and its partner space agencies to address real-world challenges on Earth and in space. Space Apps Challenge is an innovative NASA incubation program held annually. The program brings together thousands of people from around the world, who work with NASA’s open data over a 48-hour period. Space Apps is administered by the Earth Science Division of the Science Mission Directorate at NASA Headquarters in Washington, DC.
